Operationalizing ODA with composable and AI-enabled BSS
TM Forum's Open Digital Architecture (ODA) defines the blueprint for modular, composable telecom IT. The challenge for CSPs is turning this blueprint into intelligent, production-ready systems. Spotlight: New generation intelligent operations whitepaper 4.0 launch: Real change shaping the new paradigm
Please note this session is by invitation only. You can express your interest in attending by registering here.
AgenticOps represents a move away from rules-based automation toward AI agents that can perceive, reason and act with greater autonomy. Join us for the launch of TM Forum's New Generation Intelligent Operations 4.0 Whitepaper: Real change shaping the new paradigm to learn how AgenticOps are driving a shift in telcos' operations and maintenance (O&M) models.
In intelligent O&M, AI agents are positioned as "digital employees" that collaborate with human engineers. The focus is on augmenting decision-making, improving execution speed and handling increasing network complexity. Platforms and underlying technologies - including data foundations, AI frameworks and cross-domain orchestration - are critical enablers of this transformation. Without unified platforms, intelligent O&M remains fragmented and difficult to scale. Join our expert speakers to learn how intelligent automation and observability platforms can help communications service providers (CSPs) cut costs, accelerate fault resolution and transform customer experience.
Moderator: Mark Newman, Chief Analyst, TM Forum

Frank Jiao, General Manager, Intelligent Operation Domain, Huawei

Serkan Cebi, Network Operations Director, Türkiye & Europe Cluster, Vodafone
Panel: From copilots to autonomy: How to scale AgenticOps and realize true value.
There is no single path to AgenticOps, and CSPs are progressing at very different speeds on their journeys. Our case studies show that while some operators are already achieving a high degree of automation (e.g., large-scale auto-resolution of faults), others are deliberately taking their time and keeping human validation in the loop. This panel discussion will examine:
Where should operators draw the line today between assistive AI (copilots), human-in-the-loop AI and fully autonomous agents, and how will that line shift over time?
What are the risks of moving too fast versus too slowly?
Is the main bottleneck to scaling AgenticOps data quality and integration; legacy systems and silos; or processes, skills and operating model?
Which metrics matter most: MTTR, productivity improvements and cost savings, customer experience measures like NPS and CSAT, or something else?

Autonomy unleashed: Scaling level-4 networks and achieving the Dark NOC
After seeing what full-scale Dark NOC operations can achieve, this perspective asks a more uncomfortable question: where does the rest of the industry really stand today? Drawing on live autonomous network deployments, join us as we explore the gap between ambition and execution, and what operators must prioritize next to move from pockets of automation to scaled Level-4 autonomy.

Through this exchange, gain a clearer sense of where the industry is aligned, where it isn't, where CSPs agree and disagree, and what practical steps operators should be taking next to move from ambition to execution.
Is the Dark NOC the right north star for all operators - or only some?

The telecom industry has invested heavily in AI, yet many deployments remain domain-specific and operationally fragmented, lacking the real-time business context, cross-domain coordination, and operational validation needed for trusted autonomy. This session explores why the next barrier to autonomous networks is not AI insight alone, but AI's ability to coordinate, execute, and validate actions across complex, multi-vendor environments. It also requires greater standardization in how agents communicate, exchange context, trigger workflows, and operate across vendor and domain boundaries. Through use cases such as closed-loop network optimization, SLA assurance, and automated incident resolution, we will demonstrate how autonomous agents can detect issues, assess service and customer impact, perform root-cause analysis, trigger targeted testing, execute corrective actions, and validate outcomes in a continuous feedback loop, enabling more adaptive, resilient, and self-optimizing networks.
